div.div:
praeter-fĕro , no
I.perf., lātum, ferre, v. a., to carry by or past.—Pass., to come, run, drive, or fly past (rare, not in Cic.): “latebras eorum praeterlata acies est,” Liv. 21, 55, 9 : “pars vocum praeterlata,” Lucr. 4, 569 (Lachm. separately, praeter lata).
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
